text:
Maxim Shabanov's Islanders stint came apart after 44 games last season. Minnesota signed him on a one-year deal, and he has repaid it fast: nine goals and 14 points in 23 games, nine of the points on the power play, where he's on the ice for 72% of the Wild's chances, up from 27% on Long Island.

He's hot, and partly for good reason. Five goals in his last ten, on more chances than usual: 2.6 expected goals on his own shots against 2.1. That's earned.

The finishing is the part that won't last. He's shooting 25%, against 9% last season, nine goals on 5.1 expected. The chances are real; that rate rarely holds.

Five on five is the weak spot. Minnesota takes 47.5% of expected goals with him on, and does about six points better without him. For a 5-foot-9 undrafted forward who scored 67 points in his last KHL season with Traktor Chelyabinsk, the power play is the door into the lineup.

What to watch: the Wild have won five straight. When his shooting cools, his even-strength play decides how much ice he keeps.
headline: Shabanov is a power-play finisher, for now
